messages:
Jessica S: @eng-sre escalating: ACME reporting bad p95/p99 regressions hitting our Dedicated pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3. They see p95 ~2-4s but p99 spikes to 8-12s and intermittent 503s with 'attach_timeout'. Sample request ids: req=abc123, req=def456. Repro curl: ```curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-embed\",\"input\":\"test\"}'``` We opened INC-7892, customer is pretty upset, asking for ETA.

Maya (eng-sre): Looking at infra metrics now. Attach latency p95=1.8s, p99=9.4s for that pool in last 30m. Autoscaler scale-up events delayed ~45-60s between detection and effective capacity; attach worker pool saturated. Heap of concurrent attach requests - backlog spikes up. I see many simultaneous createAttachedGPU RPCs.

Tom H: Quick note - our backoff is exponential but currently no jitter. When many clients retry at same schedule that synchronizes and overloads attach workers. Also noticed attach queue length triggers only after queue=200 which is too high for this pool's worker throughput.

Alin K: Cold GPU startup times show median ~22s and 90th ~28s in that region. If attach is blocked for ~30s we get p99 cascades. Immediate mitigations: 1) bump pool target +2 GPUs, 2) route heavy traffic from ACME to fallback smaller-instance model for a few minutes, 3) enable extra prefix-caching TTL to reduce attach frequency.

Maya (eng-sre): I'll do a manual scaleup now. Command I'm running: ```infractl pool scale --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3 --delta 2 --reason \"urgent p99 surge from ACME\"```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scaling job submitted: id=scale-202603151203, status=initiated

support-bot: support-bot: ACME notified that we're applying mitigations and will follow up in ~10m. Created internal ticket INC-7892 and customer-facing note.

Tom H: For quick win we should add jitter to attach retry path. Current config: backoff base=1s max=8s, no jitter. Proposed small patch: full jitter with randomized window per request; also reduce attach-trigger threshold from 200->100 on that pool type.

Maya (eng-sre): Rolling a small canary now with jitter enabled in autoscaler. Config snippet I'm applying: ```yaml
autoscaler:
  backoff:
    type: full_jitter
    base_ms: 100
    max_ms: 8000
    jitter_pct: 0.3
  attach_queue_threshold: 100
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout to eu-west-1-dedicated-3: 10% hosts. rollout_id=canary-20260315-11. Status=started.

Alin K: Observability note: correlate per-customer attach_rate spikes - ACME's client sends 20-30 concurrent attempts within 2s when feature toggle flips. We should add per-customer attach gating + a prewarm handshake to smooth bursts.

Tom H: Longer term items: 1) async attach pipeline to decouple API threads from attach blocking, 2) attach-side caching for recent prefixes, 3) prewarm policy for high-TPS customers and 4) per-customer quotas. I'll start a PR for jitter and attach_queue threshold change. PR: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4212|pr#4212>

Maya (eng-sre): Update: after scale + canary we see p99 drop from ~9.4s -> ~3.1s within 7m. Attach queue drained, worker saturation reduced. ACME confirmed improvement. I'll keep monitoring for 30m.

Jessica S: Customer acknowledges improvement and will hold off escalation. I'll keep ticket INC-7892 open and post status.

Maya (eng-sre): Action items: 1) follow-up RFC for autoscaler jitter & prewarm (assign to eng-runtime), 2) add per-customer attach quotas & dashboard, 3) permanent change: lower attach trigger threshold for dedicated pools. Tagging @eng-runtime and @oncall to watch next 2 hours in case p99 regresses above 6s.

Tom H: Oncall, please keep an eye for p99 > 6s and escalate if we see repeat pattern. I'll open the jitter PR now. :thumbsup:

support-bot: support-bot: Noted — monitoring window started, alerts adjusted for this pool.
